== Overview ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-13-threshold|[[Dreadgods]] are colossal, nearly immortal monsters characterized by an insatiable [[hunger]] to devour the world. They possess immense power, capable of leveling mountains or destroying entire valleys simply through their movement or presence, often treating [[inhabitants]] like insignificant insects. While they are powerful enough to rival [[Monarchs]], they are considered nearly impossible to kill; even a lethal attack may only serve to awaken the other three of their kind. Their spiritual essence is composed of complex, woven threads of [[madra]] that integrate with their physical forms. There are four known [[Dreadgods]], including the [[Bleeding Phoenix]] and the [[Wandering Titan]]. They are often accompanied by cults—such as [[Redmoon Hall]]—consisting of followers who seek power through fragments of the [[Dreadgods]], like [[Blood Shadows]]. These cultists often act as scavengers or servants to their masters. A central figure in their history is [[Subject One]], also known as the Father of Hunger or the [[Slumbering Wraith]]. This entity is considered the progenitor or the first product of experiments that led to the creation of the [[Dreadgods]]. It is believed that a specific [[labyrinth]] serves as either the birthplace of these creatures or a site where they were studied, and it is a primary objective for [[Dreadgods]] to return to this location.}}

== Skysworn ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-04-skysworn|As an incomprehensibly vast creature that took to the sky, a Dreadgod represents a potential threat capable of killing everyone. This major entity causes [[Bloodspawn|bloodspawn]] to spread and utilizes servants to weaken individuals before it fully awakens. During its ascent, the creature emitted a bloody light so bright that it strengthened the [[Blood Shadow]] parasite, though [[Yerin]] was able to cut [[Bloodspawn|bloodspawn]] away from its form. Despite its sickle-like beak and the power of its scream, a Dreadgod's body can be temporarily destroyed by [[Monarchs]].}}

== Wintersteel ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-08-wintersteel|As a unique entity capable of being removed through [[Penance]], the Dreadgod represents a potential interruption to the [[tournament]] and serves as the only being within a thousand miles able to oppose [[Timaias Adama|Adama]]. This creature possesses unique [[madra]] and divine techniques, with its will even capable of lending strength to an [[Enforcer technique]]. While [[Mercy]] warns [[Akura Pride|Pride]] against provoking such a being, the [[Abyssal Palace]] prepares for its arrival as it is expected to rise within weeks. The Dreadgod's home territory is prepared for its awakening, at which point it will head toward [[Sacred Valley]] and [[Lindon]]'s home. Upon its movement, the creature's [[Spiritual pressure|spiritual pressure]] crashes over [[the Valley]] amidst a battle that becomes increasingly overwhelming.}}

== Bloodline ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-09-bloodline|While feeding at [[Sky's Edge]], the mountain-sized Dreadgod began moving slowly through the mountains toward [[Lindon]]'s homeland. This insane [[sacred beast]] cast a massive [[Shadow|shadow]] over the landscape and released power that overwhelmed all [[aspects]] of [[vital aura]], causing the [[earth aura]] to shift and the ground to shake. As it cleared a path through the mountains, its sheer presence threatened [[Lindon]]'s family and forced [[Akura family cloudship|Akura cloudships]] to flee. The creature unleashed [[blood]]-red lightning and [[Sword-aspect madra|sword-madra]] slashes, focusing its yellow-eyed gaze on a new figure after being struck by a lance of bright [[Red madra|red madra]] and the [[Hollow King]]'s Spear. Following a confrontation in [[Sacred Valley]] where its tail fell upon [[Lindon]], the Dreadgod was gone.}}

== Reaper ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|The presence of a Dreadgod is a catastrophic event that the [[Blackflame Empire]] would certainly notice. During its rampage, the entity's massive footsteps were powerful enough to shake even a tiny pond, and its destructive path left behind [[Remnants]] in the [[Sacred Valley]]. While [[Ziel of the Wasteland|Ziel]] expressed that he had no intention of fighting such a creature, it is known that engaging a Dreadgod requires immense exertion. Following the initial attack, [[Elder Whisper]] noted that no one had entered or exited [[labyrinth|the labyrinth]]. Furthermore, should a [[suppression field]] lose its power, there is a risk that the Dreadgod might return.}}

== Dreadgod ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-11-dreadgod|Known as the [[Silent King]] and the tiger of the [[Silent Servants]] cult, this self-aware Dreadgod stalked forward toward a new lair in a dark cave located three hundred miles southwest of [[Lindon]]. Although this specific entity was the least-powerful on its own, it sought slaves rather than victory and could assist in freeing powerful spirits. During a confrontation where its presence was felt near [[Yerin]], the Dreadgod's will was wrestled against by others and it launched a mental assault on [[Lindon]]. While stolen power can temporarily hold back such a being, the Dreadgod was ultimately shot through the head with [[Blackflame]] and killed by [[Lindon]]. Following this death, [[Lindon]] intended to use the creature's heart as a weapon, and [[Wei Shi Lindon Arelius]] came to be considered the fourth Dreadgod.}}

== Waybound ==
{{spoiler|book=cradle-12-waybound|[[Dreadgods]] are immense opponents characterized by a furious will and the ability to generate illusions or alter the colors of the sky through their [[aura]]. [[Weeping Dragon|The Weeping Dragon]] is identified as one such entity, and it is noted that these beings cannot be exhausted or outlasted in combat. During a confrontation, lightning snaked from the Dreadgod to feed on [[Lindon]], even as the [[Archlord|Archlords]] found themselves in its presence. Ultimately, two [[Dreadgods]] died simultaneously after their wills were utilized to haul [[Lindon]] through space via a horn, leaving behind the possibility that [[inhabitants]] of a new world might actually be [[Dreadgods]] in human form.}}

== Notable quotes ==
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-04-skysworn|“That depends,” Eithan said, “on whether or not there's a Dreadgod coming to kill us all.”<ref name="cradle-04-skysworn-c7" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-04-skysworn|"Just cut them off from the mother," Yerin said, then winced. "...the Dreadgod."<ref name="cradle-04-skysworn-c17" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-08-wintersteel|“Try to be safe. Don’t poke any Dreadgods.”<ref name="cradle-08-wintersteel-c5" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-09-bloodline|“What we did learn is that the Dreadgods are unable to retrieve their prize, even without our intervention, and will soon forget its location and return to their random wandering.<ref name="cradle-09-bloodline-c14" />}}
* {{spoiler|book=cradle-10-reaper|“I was aware the Titan was going to wake up, but then there was a second Dreadgod, and then Monarchs fought on my western border.<ref name="cradle-10-reaper-c5" />}}
